title: Juniper and the Wolf
premise: Paloma Villalobos survives in the walled city of Ceniza by stealing memories and selling them as charms, hiding the wolf-blooded magic he was born with ever since the realms sealed their covenant shut. When a dying stranger presses a map of the thirteen moon-gates into his hands, Paloma learns he is heir to the Wolf, one of three guardians whose broken oaths severed the mortal world from the wild realm—and that the seal's collapse will devour both unless a new covenant is forged before the thirteenth full moon. Hunted by the city's memory-priests and shadowed by Juniper, a fox-spirit who claims to have known his mother, Paloma gathers the scattered tokens of the old oath while confronting the truth that his mother did not abandon him but sacrificed herself to buy him time. At the final gate, Paloma refuses to restore the old covenant and instead writes a new one in his own name, choosing belonging over inheritance and binding the realms open rather than sealed.
about_author: Jonah Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a small adobe house where he claims the coyotes critique his drafts nightly.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Paloma lifts a memory of first snowfall from a grieving widow and sells it to a merchant who wants to feel something. His POV establishes Ceniza's magic ban, his charm trade, and his careful invisibility. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence—he touches other people's pasts because he cannot bear his own.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A bleeding man collapses into Paloma's rented room, pressing a leather map into his hands and whispering 'the thirteenth turn' before dying. Priests of the Memory Office arrive searching; Paloma barely escapes through the rooftops. His POV. Emotional beat: terror—the invisible life he built shatters in a single night.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: Hiding in the aqueduct tunnels, Paloma studies the map: thirteen gates circling the city, each marked with a sigil that makes his stolen memories burn hot when he nears it. He realizes the sigils respond to his blood. His POV. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity curdling into dread as inheritance stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: A fox with mismatched eyes follows Paloma for two days before speaking—Juniper, a spirit from the wild realm who knew his mother Lira and calls him 'cub.' She warns the gates are waking and the priests are hunting the map's bearer. Alternating POV begins. Emotional beat: wary wonder; the first creature in years who knows what he is.

chapters.title: The First Gate: Ash
chapters.summary: At the ash gate beneath the tannery district, Paloma's blood opens a seam showing the wild realm's edge—a forest growing sideways. A memory-priest named Brother Ossian nearly catches them; Juniper tears the map corner free. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: exhilaration poisoned by guilt—he liked using the magic.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Paloma steals a memory from Ossian himself and finds images of his own mother being interrogated five years ago—she gave up another guardian's name to protect him. Shaken, he lies to Juniper about what he saw. Dual POV; Ossian's chapter shows the Office's doctrine: magic is debt, and debts are collected. Emotional beat: shame and the first crack in his self-image.

chapters.title: The Salt Market Bargain
chapters.summary: To reach the salt gate, Paloma trades a charm containing his happiest childhood memory to a fence—unwittingly selling proof of his identity. The buyer is an informant for the Office. Juniper's POV reveals she is under her own geas: guide the cub or lose her name. Emotional beat: sacrifice and foreshadowed betrayal.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, Twelve Moons
chapters.summary: Juniper explains the covenant: three guardians—Wolf, Stag, and Owl—sealed the realms to stop a devouring thing called the Hollowing, but the seal decays each lunar turn. Paloma is the Wolf's heir; the Owl's heir is already dead. His POV. Emotional beat: the crushing arithmetic of a deadline and a duty he never asked for.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sold the Sky
chapters.summary: Seeking the Stag's heir, they find Marisol, a sky-chart seller who doesn't know her own bloodline. Convincing her means revealing magic she's spent her life denying. Marisol POV. Emotional beat: recognition between two people taught to hate what they are; fragile alliance formed.

chapters.title: Brother Ossian's Mercy
chapters.summary: Ossian corners Paloma but offers a deal instead of arrest: surrender the map and the Office will erase his wolf-blood entirely—a painless amputation of self. Paloma almost accepts. Ossian POV deepens his grief for a sister lost to unlicensed magic. Emotional beat: temptation of forgetting versus the terror of becoming.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the River
chapters.summary: Paloma, Juniper, and Marisol open the river gate together; inside, Paloma meets an echo of his mother left in the covenant's stone, which shows him the night she gave herself to the Hollowing's prison to delay its feeding. His POV. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve—she didn't leave him; she left him a job.

chapters.title: What Juniper Owes
chapters.summary: Marisol discovers Juniper's geas: the fox was sent by the Hollowing itself to deliver the cub to the final gate. Confrontation in the bone orchard; Juniper admits she chose the mission hoping to defect. Juniper POV. Emotional beat: betrayal, then forgiveness earned—not given—recasting found family as chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: The City Remembers
chapters.summary: The Office, tipped by the charm buyer, raids the salt market and publicly burns a memory-thief, turning the city against anyone touched by magic. Paloma watches a crowd he once served scream for blood. His POV. Emotional beat: disillusionment—invisibility was always complicity.

chapters.title: Ossian's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to execute captured Marisol, Ossian instead frees her, haunted by his sister's face in hers. He gives Paloma the Office's true plan: let the seal fail, then harvest the flood of wild magic as a weapon. Ossian POV. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the price of everything he believed.

chapters.title: The Stag's Token
chapters.summary: In the highlands, Marisol claims the Stag's antler-token from a shrine only her blood can open—but claiming it shows her every future in which she dies holding the line. Marisol POV. Emotional beat: courage as a decision made knowing the cost, not despite it.

chapters.title: Twelve Moons Full
chapters.summary: With one turn remaining, the group reaches the twelfth gate and finds it already torn open from the outside—the Hollowing leaking through, wearing shapes of everyone's dead. Paloma nearly drowns in a false memory of his mother forgiving him. His POV. Emotional beat: horror of comfort; learning to distrust easy absolution.

chapters.title: The Price of the Owl
chapters.summary: The covenant requires three heirs; the Owl's line is extinct. Juniper reveals the loophole: a willing spirit can stand as the third signatory, forfeiting her name and form forever. She volunteers. Juniper POV. Emotional beat: love expressed as irrevocable self-gift, and Paloma's refusal to accept it.

chapters.title: Storm Over Ceniza
chapters.summary: The Office marches on the final gate to seize the failing seal; Ossian turns his fellow priests' own memory-craft against them, buying the trio time at terrible personal cost. Multiple POVs interleave. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice rippling outward—the covenant was never one person's burden.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Gate
chapters.summary: At the moonlit summit, the Hollowing offers Paloma his mother whole if he simply lets the seal die. He sees through it—his mother's real echo appears and tells him the covenant was always meant to be rewritten by each generation. His POV. Emotional beat: the climax of identity—refusing both the inherited oath and the offered escape.

chapters.title: A Covenant in His Own Name
chapters.summary: Paloma writes new terms: the realms bound open but guarded, magic lawful and accountable, the Hollowing fed by willing shared memory instead of stolen souls. Marisol signs as Stag; Juniper prepares to be the Owl. His POV. Emotional beat: authorship—inheritance transformed into choice.

chapters.title: The Name She Keeps
chapters.summary: As Juniper speaks the Owl's vow, Paloma intervenes with a clause no one foresaw: a covenant made in his name can name its guardians, and he names her 'Juniper,' anchoring her identity within the pact itself. She keeps her name and gains a permanent place between realms. Dual POV. Emotional beat: triumph of belonging over erasure.

chapters.title: Wolf at the Door
chapters.summary: Months later, Ceniza has garden-mages and honest charm-shops; Paloma runs a school teaching memory-ethics, Marisol charts living skies, and Ossian tends the archives he once policed. On the thirteenth turn, Paloma walks the open gate as its Wolf and comes home to friends. His POV closes the book. Emotional beat: quiet joy—belonging finally chosen, kept, and shared.
